    odd = sum(1 for x in arr if x % 2 == 1)
    even = n - odd
    
    actions = 0
    while odd > 0 and even > 0:
        if odd >= 2:
            # pair two odds to make an even
            odd -= 2
            even += 1
            actions += 1
        else:
            # odd == 1
            odd -= 1
            even -= 1
            odd += 1  # sum is odd
            actions += 1
    print(actions)

from functools import lru_cache

def solve():
    import sys
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
    n = data[0]
    nums = data[1:]
    a = sum(1 for x in nums if x % 2 == 1)
    b = n - a
    
    @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
    def dp(odd, even):
        if odd == 0 or even == 0:
            return 0
        best = 0
        # odd + even = odd
        if odd >= 1 and even >= 1:
            best = max(best, 1 + dp(odd, even - 1))
        # odd + odd = even
        if odd >= 2:
            best = max(best, 1 + dp(odd - 2, even + 1))
        # even + even = even
        if even >= 2:
            best = max(best, 1 + dp(odd, even - 1))
        return best
    
    print(dp(a, b))

solve()

import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return

    n = int(data[0])
    a = list(map(int, data[1:1+n]))

    odd = sum(x & 1 for x in a)
    even = n - odd

    # An action is possible iff there is at least one odd and one even ball.
    # The only usable pair is (odd, even), whose sum is odd.
    # So each action decreases the number of even balls by 1 and keeps odd >= 1.
    # Hence the maximum number of actions is exactly the initial number of even balls.
    print(even)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
